title: SFL Annotations with LLM CLI Coding Agents

questions.prompt: Which CLI coding agents should be supported as SFL annotation backends?
questions.description: Each agent has distinct CLI flags for headless execution and structured output (e.g., vibe -p, agy -p, claude -p, opencode run).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Unified adapter layer supporting vibe, agy, claude, and opencode with a shared interface.

options.label: All four: vibe, agy, claude, opencode via an extensible adapter interface

questions.prompt: How should clauses/utterances be batched when invoking CLI agents?
questions.description: Spawning an external CLI process per individual clause causes high process overhead and latency for large transcripts. Batching amortizes startup time.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Batch at the parent chunk level (all clauses of a parent chunk in one CLI invocation), with single-clause fallback.

options.label: Default to parent-chunk batching with single-clause fallback and configurable batch size
Strict parent-chunk batching only (group all clauses for each parent chunk in one prompt)
Per-clause invocation (one CLI call per child clause, identical to existing DSPy loop)

questions.prompt: What SFL linguistic dimensions should the CLI agent annotate?
questions.description: Current pipeline runs deterministic spaCy pass-1 (participants, processes, circumstances) followed by LLM pass-2 (mood, modality, tenor).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Hybrid: Keep deterministic spaCy pass 1 for syntactic base, pass it to CLI agent for interpersonal analysis (mood, modality, tenor) and ideational validation.

options.label: Hybrid: Deterministic spaCy pass 1 + CLI agent pass 2 (mood, modality, tenor) with ideational validation
Pass 2 only: CLI agent strictly generates {mood, modality, tenor}
Full Agent SFL: CLI agent produces both ideational (participants, processes) and interpersonal tags directly

questions.prompt: Where should the CLI agent SFL annotator be exposed in the application?
questions.description: How users and system workflows trigger and select the CLI agent backend.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Integrate into the core SFL engine factory (used by TUI and web server) and provide a dedicated CLI command.

options.label: Core Engine Factory: Configurable via settings/env for transparent use in TUI and Web Corpus Explorer
Dedicated CLI Command: e.g. 'notebooklm corpus sfl' or 'notebooklm sfl annotate'
Standalone Python API: Exportable AgentSFLEngine class for scripts and custom pipelines

questions.prompt: How should agent invocation failures, process timeouts, or malformed JSON be handled?
questions.description: External CLI processes may encounter timeouts, rate limits, or non-zero exit codes.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Configurable retry with JSON repair, with optional fallback to DSPy or graceful error recording per clause.

options.label: Retry with JSON repair, optional fallback to default DSPy engine if agent fails
Fail immediately: record error on the clause/parent and report without falling back
Record neutral placeholder annotations on failure without aborting the rest of the run
